[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] A wave of molasses once crushed Boston. It sounds like a joke, but it was real and it killed twenty-one people. January fifteenth, nineteen nineteen, an oddly warm day. A huge tank by the harbor held over two million gallons. Just after noon, its rivets popped like machine gun fire. Then a wave up to twenty-five feet tall tore loose. It rushed through the streets at about thirty-five miles an hour, bending the elevated railway and flattening whole buildings. Courts blamed the company, and building rules got stricter. Locals swore the street smelled sweet on hot days for decades.
